claims.text: The Pulumi for Terraform Users guide teaches how to reference existing Terraform state files from Pulumi, use any Terraform provider in Pulumi programs, import and use Terraform modules directly, convert HCL to Pulumi, and orchestrate Terraform and Pulumi deployments together.
Any Terraform provider can be used in Pulumi programs.
Terraform modules can be imported and used directly in Pulumi.

Pulumi provides a `terraform.state.S3Reference` resource (in @pulumi/terraform, also referenced as `pulumi.terraform.state.S3Reference`) taking `bucket` and `key` arguments to reference Terraform state stored in S3, with a `getOutput` method.
`pulumi.StackReference` takes a stack name and exposes `getOutput` to read another stack's outputs.
`aws.ecs.Cluster` accepts `configuration.executeCommandConfiguration` with `kmsKeyId` and `logging: "DEFAULT"` arguments.
`pulumi import` can be used to bring Terraform-managed resources under Pulumi management.
`pulumi import <type> <name> <id>` syntax with types such as `aws:ec2/vpc:Vpc`, `aws:ec2/subnet:Subnet`, `aws:ecs/cluster:Cluster` imports existing resources into Pulumi.
`@pulumi/policy` exports `PolicyPack` and `validateResourceOfType`, and PolicyPack policies accept `name`, `description`, `enforcementLevel: "mandatory"`, and `validateResource`.
Pulumi policies can enforce infrastructure policies across both Terraform and Pulumi resources.
`aws.s3.Bucket` has an `acl` property that can be read in a policy validation with values "public-read" and "public-read-write".

`@pulumi/pulumi/automation` exports `LocalWorkspace.createOrSelectStack` taking `stackName`, `projectName`, and an inline `program`; stacks have `setConfig` and `up({ onOutput })`, and `up` results have `outputs`.
The Automation API lets you embed Pulumi in applications for dynamic infrastructure management.
Component resources can be created that integrate with Terraform behind the scenes, leaving multi-tool complexity to the platform team rather than development teams.
`pulumi.ComponentResource` subclasses call `super(type, name, {}, opts)` and `registerOutputs` with `pulumi.ComponentResourceOptions`.

`aws.lb.LoadBalancer`, `aws.ecs.TaskDefinition`, and `aws.ecs.Service` accept properties such as `loadBalancerType`, `internal`, `requiresCompatibilities`, `networkMode: awsvpc`, `cpu`, `memory`, `containerDefinitions`, `launchType`, `networkConfiguration.assignPublicIp`.
